title: Lunatic Judgment
text: “Yuki, I don’t have one for you. Well, maybe I’ll make one next time if I’m really free.”
“What an arrogant dragon you are!”
“Yeah, yeah, yeah!”

Since then, things have been going along without any major issues. I hear that Ren and Itsuki are getting along well with Fleon-chan and Black Thunder. Based on intel from me and my Rival, we’re also heading to the villages and towns where the reincarnated folks have set up their strongholds to investigate whether the rumors are true. It seems the training regimen for Big Sister Itsuki has become quite extensive, which does make me a little worried. Well, since Kou is with her, there’s probably no need to worry.
“Still… both the Sword Hero and the Bow Hero have such different personalities.”
“They’re really full of life, aren’t they?”
“It’d be more accurate to say they’re giddy… No, maybe that’s their liberation from all worldly ties. This is what true pity looks like.”
Rival said something in a way that seemed to look down on Ren and Itsuki. Since we don’t have to waste time trying to persuade them, that’s one less hassle to deal with.
Right now, we’re witnessing Ren take down a reincarnated person.
“I’ve seen through your darkness…”
“Darkness returns to darkness!”
That’s the kind of vibe Ren gave off as he drew his sword against the reincarnated one and his pig-like minions. Black Thunder’s right there with him, too.
“Just because you’re a hero doesn’t mean you can get all high and mighty! Haaaaaaaaaaah!”
The reincarnated one picked a fight with Ren, spouted some wild nonsense, and—convinced he could win—charged right at him.

If I recall correctly, this time she found out Ren was the Hero, came to a quiet street, bumped into him as they passed each other, and started a fight over how her medicinal herbs were ruined. Ren told her that if she wanted those herbs so badly, he’d give them to her—and right then and there, he pulled a bunch of dropped items from his weapon and tossed them at her. But she started making a fuss, claiming that these were the very herbs that would save her, that there was no substitute for them, and that she couldn’t forgive him.

It’s a standard tactic for reincarnated individuals to play the victim like this. I really can’t understand why she’d carry such an important herb and then deliberately bump into Ren. From there, it escalated into a fight. She seems to think that if it comes down to a sword-to-sword clash, she’ll be able to snatch it away.
“Your lunge was too weak!”
Zuuuaa! Ren brought his sword down on the reincarnated individual, then swept upward, sending her flying.
“Ugh!?”
“Zweite Tornado!”
Black Thunder summoned a tornado and flung the reincarnated one upward again to keep him from falling.
“‘Buhiiiiii!?’”
The pig henchmen were swept up by the tornado along with him.
“Chain Bind V!”
With a clatter, the chains from Ren’s restraint skill were unleashed upon the reincarnated warriors, binding them tightly. By the way, Chain Bind is a skill equivalent to Father’s Shield Prison.
“Haaaaaaaaaaah!”
Ren’s sword glowed brightly as he leaped high into the air. Then, mid-air, he launched a sharp thrust toward the reincarnated warrior.
“Lunatic Judgment III!”
“Ugh!?”
With a thunderous thud, Ren’s thrust flew through the air in the shape of a bird, piercing the reincarnated warriors and causing a massive explosion.
“Guaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!?”
The reincarnated warriors were engulfed by the explosion and fell to the ground, charred black.
“‘Buhiiiiii!?’ ””
The pigs were caught in the blast wave of Ren’s Lunatic Judgment, took massive damage, and collapsed just like the reincarnated one.
“Hmph… Return to the darkness.”
“Well then, there is no darkness here. There’s no point in staying any longer.”
Following Black Thunder’s words, Ren struck a victory pose.
“I’ll leave it to you then! Time Drive!”
“Here we go!”
Renn mounted Black Thunder’s back and rode off with a dashing flourish. It’s great to see them getting along so well.

Next up is Itsuki. While helping the Big Sisters with their training, he apparently hunts down reincarnated souls whenever he finds a moment to spare. It seems he operates on a schedule that makes full use of Fleon-chan’s mobility. In Itsuki’s case, he thoroughly investigates the reincarnated souls’ backgrounds before catching them red-handed at the scene of the crime and confronting them. I ended up accompanying him to the scene as the Filolial Mask.
What were the charges against this reincarnated person again? Ah, right—apparently, they raided a Beastman settlement, killed the inhabitants, and served their flesh as food.

Even in Melromarc, I’m told there’s no culture of eating Beastmen. Even though they possess beast-like traits, they’re still human, after all. I suppose people get all up in a fuss about ethics and such.

Apparently, since the villagers were suffering from starvation, they initially thought it was monster meat. However, once they realized it was the flesh of Beastmen living in a nearby forest, their faces turned pale, and then they flew into a rage. Wild boars, bears… and dog-like Beastmen similar to Keel, I’m told. They had been trading with them, and apparently, they ate people they’d spoken with just a few months earlier without even realizing it. It’s a sickening story. To put it in human terms, it’s like the gory version of “Kachikachi Yama.” The Tanuki plays Big Sister… no, let’s drop that idea for the sake of Big Sister’s honor.

When this was reported to the kingdom, the intervention of a noble pig from the kingdom ensured no charges were filed, and the person who made the accusation was the one who ended up in prison. Of course, there are all sorts of stories about how they couldn’t let the children know about it. Fleon-chan and Itsuki gathered this information from various sources, which led them to track down the reincarnated individuals.

“What you’ve done is nothing short of mass murder! If you were to be properly punished according to the kingdom’s laws, that would be one thing… but currying favor with those in power and doing as you please… We, the Filolial Masks, will act on behalf of the Hero and Heaven to send you on your way!”

“That’s right… Killing defenseless people, feeding them to innocent villagers without their knowledge, and causing suffering to good people without facing punishment—even if it was a misunderstanding—is utterly outrageous… You can still atone for your sins.”
“Y-yes! The sin of cannibalism is unforgivable!”
“Are you guys the heroes everyone’s been talking about? Why the hell do I have to be treated like the villain?!”

It seems the reincarnated ones don’t truly believe, from the bottom of their hearts, that their actions were evil. By the way, although they’re categorized as “reincarnated,” there are also those among them who, like us, came to this world through transfer. Cola is one such example.
“I stated the reason earlier. Even if they’re Beastmen, they’re still human. We’re arresting you for the crime of massacring the indigenous people!”
“Ha! What charges are you even talking about?!”
“Right here… With the official seal of approval from various nations, you’re already wanted criminals!”

Fleon-chan thrusts the poster forward with a dramatic “Ta-da!” She’s used her authority as a hero to dig up what the reincarnated ones and that pig had covered up using their power, and officially accepted it as valid.
“W-What! I’m not going to put up with this kind of frame-up! All right then! Let’s give these self-righteous jerks a taste of their own medicine!”
“Oink!”
The reincarnated one drew his weapon and lunged toward us.
“Let’s get this over with! Mr. Justice! Ms. Leiska! No. 1!”
“Leave it to me!”
“It’s not enough to trouble you all… Shock Arrow IV… Bind Arrow III.”

Tatan! With a clatter, Itsuki generated three arrows aimed at the reincarnated warrior and the pig, fired them into the ground to make them ricochet, and then fired another arrow to pin them in midair.
“Ugh!? Guaaaaaaaah!?”
“Oinkkkk!?”
Then he leaped high into the air and drew his bow back with all his might. The bow glowed brightly, and light gathered onto the arrow.
“Lunatic Judgment III!”

With a sharp “Bam,” Itsuki released the arrow, which took the shape of a bird, pierced the reincarnated ones, and exploded. Of course, just like during Ren’s battle, the reincarnated ones were charred black and collapsed to the ground.
“We did it! Now let’s tie them up and hand them over to the proper authorities! The government will surely mete out their punishment!”
“Waaah…”
Leiska lets out a pitiful whimper, but she goes about tying up the reincarnated ones with practiced ease. It seems she has no doubts whatsoever about justice.
“They haven’t caused enough trouble yet! Aren’t there any others?”
“Peace is best, Number 1.”
Fleon-chan certainly has a point. That’s why I’m reluctantly holding back, too.
“I think it’d be faster to just eliminate these guys. If Fleon-chan will allow it, I’ll burn them until not even a speck of dust remains.”
“No, Number 1. That’s just the end result; the formality is what matters.”

Hmm… So in Fleon-chan’s sense of justice, form is what matters, is it? Even if the end result—getting rid of these guys—remains the same, mind you. After that, we took the captured reincarnated individuals to the country that had requested our help.
“Well then, Mr. Justice, Ms. Leiska, let’s move on to the next one. There are still so many people out there who’ve been trampled by evil and are crying out for help.”
“Yes.”
Itsuki climbed onto Fleon-chan’s back, who had transformed into her Filolial form. Then Fleon-chan clung to Leiska’s back with her feet and flapped her wings, flying off.
“Whaaaat!?”
Even heroes have a tough time, don’t they?
After that, I showed my Father the footage I’d recorded of Ren and Itsuki’s activities on a video crystal.
“Raph.”

My father is petting a Raph-type creature—a creature my Rival and I had created and already named “Raph-chan”—on his lap. There’s a certain air of dignity about him. I’ll kneel and bow my head to match the mood.
“…Motoyasu, what are you doing?”
“Just messing around, that’s all.”
“Stop that—you’re making me look like the leader of a secret evil society.”
“Understood!”
Time to stand up and salute! After that, I had Father watch the entire video.
“What did you think?”
“…It felt like ‘Lunatic Judgment.’”
“Are you interested? I can use it, too!”
I twirled my spear around to show off. I’m sure Father wants to try it out, too.
“What are the conditions?”
“You picked that up without me noticing, didn’t you?”
I really have no memory of that at all! Since I’ve never seen Ren or Itsuki use it in previous loops, there might be some special conditions involved.
“Ren and Itsuki too?”
“I don’t know that much, though. It’s just that charging this skill is a hassle. There’s no doubt it’s faster to just unleash a Brionac. I’m sure it’s the same for Ren and Itsuki.”
“So it’s one of those ‘show-off moves’… I wonder what kind of skills I’ll have.”
I sense a touch of melancholy in my Father’s demeanor.
“It’ll surely be a magnificent Lunatic Judgment.”
“It’s not like I’m feeling all that romantic about it… Wait, what am I even saying?”
My Father let out a sigh.
“So? Is it popular?”
“It’s a flashy move, after all. I’ll film it later and show it to you.”
“No need. Anyway, so Ren and Itsuki are at least doing what they’re supposed to… I hear their public image is improving too, so that’s a good thing…”
And with that, my report to my Father was over.

“Filo seems to be enjoying her idol activities with Melty… and it looks like they’re doing some ‘Merphilo’ on the side too, so I guess that’s a good thing… though I’m starting to have a bit of free time on my hands.”
“I’ll stick around to help with your training, Father.”
“Yeah, yeah. Well, now that we’ve confirmed everything, let’s get to work today.”
That’s how the report went. Oh, and I also filmed Big Sister’s training log. Father watched it with great interest while petting a Raph Seed.
Now then… we’re currently at a detention center managed by Faubrey. As for why we’re in a place like this, it’s related to the issue with Ren and Itsuki I mentioned earlier.
“Either way, heroes of justice and heroes of the darkness are just a pain in the neck.”
Rival says with a sigh. By the way, I’ve already reported this matter to Father. It’s a task he knew about but still dumped on me and Rival.

As for what’s actually going on here… the reincarnated individuals that Ren and Itsuki captured are being held here and forcibly put to sleep. It’s amazing they even bother trying to reason with these guys—it’s completely pointless. It’s already been proven that even my kind Father’s experiments were a waste of time. Reincarnators are nothing but trash incapable of reflection. After all, when public opinion turned against them and the hunt for reincarnators began, they ignored their own misdeeds and cried foul, claiming it was a “witch hunt” if they got caught. Yet despite that, they still attack us while brandishing the “might makes right” mentality—they’re truly despicable.

A common line they spout is, “I’m the strongest! Heroes are just cannon fodder!” They really have no sense of their own limitations. Ren does the same—under the guise of “dark work,” he teams up with Black Thunder to take down reincarnated individuals—but he captures about half of them alive and dumps them on the relevant parties… the shadowy underbelly of the nation—before vanishing into the shadows himself. Needless to say, due to the nature of their crimes, most of those pigs end up being sent to the Pig King. Anyway, my Father has now entrusted us with deciding what to do with the reincarnated individuals captured by Ren and Itsuki.
“Just leave the disposal of the reincarnated ones to me.”
All I have to do is deliver the finishing blow. I’ll just gather them in one place and wipe them out with a Brionac. But here, just like Fleon-chan, Rival called a halt.
“Rival, if it’s a hassle, shouldn’t I just dispose of them myself? Why are you getting in the way?”
“Well, that’s because these guys still have a use.”
A use for these guys?

“These guys are the scum of this world. My Father from the first world used to say so. Reincarnated beings are, by nature, incompetent; yet, despite that, they’re full of unfounded pride and are jealous Trash—fools who’ve been targeted by the Crimson Swine itself and are trapped in the illusion of being the ‘strongest,’ having become intoxicated by their power.”

I turn my gaze toward the unconscious reincarnated beings and say, “That’s certainly true.” These guys obsess over being the “strongest” for no good reason. As soon as someone they perceive as stronger than themselves appears, they keenly spot that person’s flaws, make a huge fuss as if it were a major problem, and pick a fight. This is exactly what it means to lay bare one’s ignorance.

Come to think of it, my Father from the first world once mentioned why the Crimson Swine itself chose to send such incompetent individuals. Apparently, aside from causing chaos in the world, there was also the aspect of wanting to reaffirm its own competence. According to my Father, it’s only natural for a capable person to be given immense power and produce results. He said that a self-proclaimed god—a walking embodiment of self-importance—could never be satisfied by granting power to such a person. If he gives power to an incompetent person and they produce results, that proves the Crimson Swine himself is competent… Apparently, that’s the meaning behind this so-called “god” bestowing power on the incompetent. And if, as a bonus, they can wreak havoc on the world, all the better, it seems. I don’t know why he’d want to do such a thing, but it seems he was getting drunk on his own power by using those foolish, incompetent reincarnated individuals.
“What value do such people have? They’re the same as Takt, aren’t they?”
“Hehe… It just goes to show that even trash has its own use. Since this was also something their brains came up with, it’s best for the global economy if they play the fools and exit the stage.”
“You’re talking in riddles.”
“Just help me take these guys away. The Zeltoble Dark Guild is full of secrets, after all.”
And so, Rival, through Father, ordered me to take the reincarnated ones to a certain island.
